Full release notes: **https://danbyte.net/news/v0-16-0**

### New in 0.16.7

#### Fixed

- **A 3D scene of a big hall loads faster.** The scene payload looked up the feed behind every power inlet one query at a time, 600 queries on a 2,400-device hall; it is two queries now.

- **New code on an old database is named, not guessed at.** A restart without the migrate step left every page that read a new column failing with `column … does not exist` and nothing saying why. `/api/health/` now reports `db_behind_code`, Settings → Updates shows the migrations still to run with the command to run them, and the log names them at startup, the mirror of the existing "code behind the database" check.

- **3D room: cable runs are readable.** A lead between two devices in one cabinet was dressed at the cabinet wall, 20 cm past the gear in an 800 mm rack, with its riser 12 cm out in the aisle, and every lead to one side shared the exact same line, so a switch with a handful of patch leads drew as horseshoes leaving the rack and merging into one crossing bundle. Runs now take the corner channel 2 cm outside the rail opening and 3 cm in front of the face, on the side nearest the two ports, each in a small lane of its own. A long same-face run takes the channel instead of a diagonal across the faceplates in between. The cable card says when an end has no port marker and is drawn at the panel centre.
- **The traced cable's marching line moves while the camera stands still.** On the on-demand render loop the crawl only advanced when something else drew a frame, so it froze until you orbited. It now keeps its own 30 Hz clock.

#### Added

- **Port labels on faceplates.** Settings → Admin → Faceplates → **Port labels** prints text inside each port marker on the rendered faceplate, the photo panel and the 3D room: the port's label, the cable's label, the far-end device or the far-end port's label, in a colour of your choosing. The text is fitted to the marker and never leaves it; the rendered cage keeps its port number above the label. A device can force labels shown or hidden; an interface can hide its own or give it a colour of its own.
- **3D room name plates that stay out of the way.** Under Device names, choose every rack or only the highlighted one, and move the plates off the gear so they start at the rail edge instead of covering the faceplate.

- **Cable thickness slider in the 3D room, and an Auto / Tubes / Lines choice.** The View menu scales every cable from a quarter to double life size, and can force every run to a shaded tube or to a flat, constant-width line in its solid colour, where Auto switched to lines past two hundred cables. Both saved per device like the quality tier.
